history.origins: Vatra (Fire) and Magarac (Jackass) are versions of Pig without a stock played in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They belong to the card-passing family; players pass cards in turn rather than simultaneously like basic Pig. Vatra uses physical punishment and is traditionally played by young boys.
timeline: 20th–21st century: Played in Bosnia and Herzegovina as youth party game.

setup.deck: Use 4 cards per player (one complete rank each). Extra deck for punishment.
setup.dealing: 4 cards each (one rank per player in deck).

rules.objective: Collect four cards of the same rank (four-of-a-kind). Be the first to slam your hand and yell 'Vatra!'; the last player to do so loses the hand and receives a suit-based physical punishment.
rules.gameplay: Pass 1 card left simultaneously. First four-of-a-kind calls 'Vatra!' Loser names a card from shuffled full deck. Winner flips cards until named card appears. Each flipped card's suit = specific penalty (â™ =hit, â™£=knuckles, â™¦=pinch, â™¥=pet).

strategy.basic: Focus on one rank. Pass off-rank cards.

variations.emptyOverridesReason: No variant overrides documented; Vatra and Magarac differ by punishment only (see rules).

scoring.winCondition: Collect four-of-a-kind first. Don't be last.
